verdict.rationale: HyperAgent's page.ai() lets developers issue natural-language commands (e.g., 'search for flights... select the cheapest option') instead of writing selectors, and docs explicitly say it lets you 'write natural language commands instead of complex selectors,' matching the DOM-understanding action-primitive story. However, evidence shows a single high-level task-execution call rather than discrete act/click/type primitives, and there's no independent/hands-on evidence confirming resilience to selector or layout changes. Missing for 10: granular primitive-level API docs (separate click/type/act calls), independent verification of survival across DOM/layout changes, and community confirmation of reliability.
